ui.title: Career Guidance Test for Civil Servants
ui.intro: This educational tool helps public administration students explore possible career paths within the system of federal executive bodies of the Russian Federation.
ui.scaleIntro: The test measures six dimensions of your professional profile:
ui.scaleLegend:
P - law enforcement, control and supervision S - social and humanitarian policy orientation E - economic, financial and market regulation
I - international and foreign-policy orientation D - digitalization, data and ICT T - territorial distribution and field-oriented work
ui.questionsTitle: How strongly do you agree with the statements below?
ui.likertNote: The questionnaire uses a Likert scale: 1 - strongly disagree, 2 - somewhat disagree, 3 - neither agree nor disagree / unsure, 4 - somewhat agree, 5 - strongly agree.
ui.completeNote: To get a valid result, answer every question.
ui.chartNote: The chart axes correspond to the six scales: P - law enforcement and control, S - social and humanitarian policy, E - economic and financial orientation, I - international orientation, D - digital technologies and data, T - territorial and field-oriented work. Values range from 1 to 5: the higher the score, the stronger the orientation.
ui.topTitle: Federal Executive Bodies Closest to Your Profile (Top 5)
ui.fullRankingTitle: Full Ranking of All Bodies (by Increasing Profile Distance)
ui.distanceNote: Distance is the squared Euclidean distance between your vector (P, S, E, I, D, T) and the institutional profile. The smaller the value, the closer the match.
ui.answerRequired: Please answer all questions before calculating the result.

questions.P1: I would be interested in participating in inspections of legal compliance and documenting violations.
questions.P2: I am comfortable in situations where rules must be enforced firmly, even if people are dissatisfied.
questions.P3: I would prefer work where I rarely have to deal with violations or conflict situations.
questions.P4: The possibility of applying administrative measures such as fines, orders or restrictions does not frighten me.
questions.P5: Strict adherence to regulations and constant paperwork in prescribed forms seems excessively tiring to me.
questions.P6: I would avoid work involving field inspections of organizations or citizens.
questions.S1: It is important to me that the results of my work directly affect people's quality of life, including income, health, education and social protection.
questions.S2: I would be interested in designing support measures for specific social groups, such as youth, families with children or older people.
questions.S3: I am more likely to choose work with people than work with technical systems or infrastructure objects.
questions.S4: Social policy seems too vague and emotional to me; I would prefer more technical tasks.
questions.S5: I am ready to regularly participate in citizen receptions, public hearings and meetings with residents.
questions.S6: Culture, education, healthcare and social support interest me less than industry, transport or energy.
questions.E1: I am interested in understanding budget indicators, taxes, tariffs and financial flows.
questions.E2: I enjoy analyzing tables with economic data, even when they are quite large.
questions.E3: I would not want my future work to be closely connected with numbers, calculations and economic indicators.
questions.E4: Regulating markets, competition and prices seems important and attractive to me.
questions.E5: Issues of state property, privatization and asset management seem boring and overly formal to me.
questions.E6: I would be interested in participating in the development of national economic policy, including tax, customs and budget policy.
questions.I1: I would like to work in a field related to international cooperation, negotiations and interstate projects.
questions.I2: I am ready to regularly use foreign languages in professional work.
questions.I3: I would be more comfortable dealing with domestic Russian issues that are not part of the international agenda.
questions.I4: I am attracted to work where international standards, agreements and practices must be taken into account.
questions.I5: Frequent trips abroad and participation in international events would tire me more than inspire me.
questions.I6: I am interested in how foreign policy and foreign economic relations affect national and regional development.
questions.D1: I am interested in working with information systems, databases and digital platforms.
questions.D2: I quickly master new digital services and software and enjoy doing so.
questions.D3: I would prefer computers and information systems to play a supporting rather than central role in my future work.
questions.D4: I would be interested in projects that digitalize public services and administrative processes.
questions.D5: Analyzing large datasets such as statistics, registries and monitoring data seems too technical and boring to me.
questions.D6: Information security, personal data protection and internet regulation seem professionally attractive to me.
questions.T1: I am comfortable regularly travelling to regions, inspecting sites and communicating with local authorities.
questions.T2: I would rather choose work where almost everything happens in one office without frequent trips around the country.
questions.T3: I am interested in seeing how federal-level decisions are implemented in specific regions and municipalities.
questions.T4: I am not attracted to working in a system with a branched network of territorial bodies and constant interaction with local managers.
questions.T5: I see the opportunity to travel extensively around Russia for work as an advantage rather than a disadvantage.
questions.T6: I would like my work to be as office-based as possible and not require site visits or local meetings.
